title: Token Chronicle Flowboard — iterative wires & notes
body:
Purpose and scope:

This note captures the design thinking and wireframe iteration ideas for a token-level timeline inspector (working name: Token Chronicle / Flowboard) — a lightweight interactive panel in Console that lets engineers and SREs replay a single invocation or an aggregated slice and see both latency and cost attribution at the token granularity. Goal: make it obvious where time and money are spent per invocation, make root-cause discovery faster, and expose levers (batching, cache hit, model variant) with drill-downs so teams can act.

Audience:
- Platform owners troubleshooting high p99 latency on Redwood Dedicated/private deployments
- Product engineers optimizing prompt templates and batching strategies
- Solutions and CS for customer postmortems and cost reviews

Design constraints / assumptions:
- We will surface trace-level data but must avoid sending full prompt text to UI by default for privacy (optionally redact or request permission).
- Must support both single-invocation replay and aggregation across N invocations (session compare).
- Backend telemetry needed: per-token timestamps (generation start/finish), kernel selection id, quantization mode, cache hit boolean, batch size, queue time, allocated GPU/instance id, token byte size, model_variant id, token_type (prompt/assistant/function), and cost weight.
- Performance: UI should stream token lanes progressively; avoid blocking on full payload for long responses.

Core interactions (sketches written as states):

1) Overview strip (compact):
- Horizontal compact timeline summarizing the whole invocation: left to right shows time.
- Overlaid heatmap: color intensity = token latency; width = token output length.
- Small stacked bar above: cost contribution per segment (prompt tokens vs generated tokens vs system calls).
- Hover shows micro-tooltip with: token index, latency (ms), cost (USD), cache_hit, kernel id.

2) Expanded lane mode (drill):
- Expand a token-range (click and drag to select a range). Opens vertical lane view: each token as a row with columns: idx | text (redacted by default) | latency bar with phase breakdown | cost | cache | kernel | batch_id | gpu_device.
- Phase breakdown slices: queue -> decode/prep -> forward -> kv-lookup -> postprocess -> send. Each slice is clickable to surface related logs/traces.

3) Replay scrubber (timeplay):
- Scrubber control that replays token emission along timeline; playing highlights which kernel and batch processed each token, shows a trailing sparkline of cumulative cost.
- Can step by token or jump to next expensive token. Useful for async debug flows.

4) Compare mode (A/B):
- Select two invocations or aggregated slices to compare token timelines side-by-side. The UI aligns tokens by role and shows delta overlays (latency delta, cost delta).
- Auto-detect alignment issues (generated text divergence) and offer fuzzy alignment mode.

5) Attribution toggles and filters:
- Toggle to aggregate by model_variant, kernel_type (fp16/int8), batch_size, cache_hit, or by shard/device.
- Filter to show only slow tokens (p95/p99), or tokens contributing top X% of cost.

6) Suggestions strip (actionable insights):
- Based on observed patterns, surface suggestions: 
  - "High queue time on calls: consider increasing reserved concurrency or enabling burst capacity for route X."
  - "First N tokens consistently have high latency due to model cold start; consider warmup or smaller context implementation."
  - "KV cache hit rate low; check prefix stability or enable prefix hashing for session IDs."
- Each suggestion should be linkable to an automatic checklist (ownership + tickets).

Wireframe progression notes (iteration log):

v0 — one-pane waterfall
- Single horizontal waterfall with per-token bars colored by latency.
- Pros: quick to build. Cons: hard to inspect phases and attribute cost precisely.

v1 — lane + phase breakdown
- Add per-token rows with phase slices.
- Introduced hover detail with links to trace IDs and log snippets.
- Learned: too dense for long responses; need lazy loading and collapsing groups.

v1.5 — grouped tokens + sparklines
- Group tokens by logical units (prompt blocks, assistant responses, function calls) and show mini-sparkline for each group.
- Add collapse/expand.

v2 — replay + compare
- Added time scrubber and A/B compare. Sticky header shows aggregated stats and top-3 tokens by cost contribution.
- Integration with 'Rollouts' page to replay requests for different model variants.

Accessibility & privacy considerations:
- Redaction toggle for prompt text: on by default in hosted mode, optional in Dedicated/Private if tenant policy allows.
- Keyboard navigation for scrubber and token focus.
- Colors use WCAG-compliant palette; heatmap scale adjustable for colorblind-safe palettes.

Data model and backend requirements (notes for infra team):
- Required per-invocation payload: invocation_id, start_ts, end_ts, list[token_index, role, token_bytes, start_ms, end_ms, phase_durations (CSV), cache_hit, kernel_id, batch_id, model_variant, device_id, cost_microunits].
- Support streaming of token events over websocket or long-poll to avoid large initial payloads.
- Aggregation API that computes "top cost tokens" for a slice without returning text.
- Storage: keep raw token-level traces for up to 7 days for live debugging, aggregated summaries for 90 days. (policy to be confirmed with privacy/retention team)

Telemetry / metrics to surface on top strip:
- total_invocations_examined, avg_token_latency, p95_token_latency, total_cost_usd, top_kernel_by_time, cache_hit_rate, average_batch_size.

Open UX questions / tradeoffs (to triage):
- Q1: Should generated token text be default-visible for host accounts? Risk of PII leakage. Recommendation: redact by default and add explicit "Reveal tokens" button with audit log.
- Q2: How to visualize large responses (10k+ tokens) without UI slowdown? Options: virtualized list + group summaries + sampling.
- Q3: Should suggestions be rule-based (deterministic) or ML-powered (pattern detection)? Start with ruleset to keep UX explainable.
- Q4: How to credit multi-model fallbacks (when system retries on smaller variant)? Need per-token model attribution.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Interactive timeline for single invocation with hover showing latency and cost per token.
- Phase breakdown visible for selected tokens with links to trace/log IDs.
- Redaction toggle for token text and audit logging on reveal.
- Basic aggregation API to compute top cost tokens for a time slice.
- Suggestions strip with three initial rules enabled.

Backlog & next steps (action items):
- [product] finalize scope for MVP and prioritize fields for telemetry schema. (Owner: Aisha)
- [infra] prototype streaming endpoint for token event stream (Owner: Marcus).
- [design] mock high-density layout and test with 3 internal SREs and 2 customers (Diego + Priya).
- [security] review redaction policy and retention timeline; confirm enterprise opt-in controls.
- [eng] spike on virtualized token list performance with 10k tokens (Jinsoo).

Meeting notes from 2025-02-18 sync with infra & SRE:
- Infra: prefer streaming for everything; raw traces are heavy but workable if we chunk. Suggested mid-term: sample full text only for flagged invocations.
- SRE: wants alignment view to compare warm vs cold runs; wants batch_id -> queue_time correlation graph out of the box.
- PM: prioritize privacy toggle and suggestion rules in first release.

Sketch quick references (for hand-off to design):
- Sketch A: compact horizontal heatstrip + top stats + small actionbar (copy trace id, open in trace explorer, reveal tokens).
- Sketch B: full lane — collapsible groups, phase bars with colored slices, right-side mini-pane for logs/context.
- Sketch C: compare view — split-screen aligned tokens with delta badges and a shared scrubber.

Prototype test plan (lightweight):
- Recruit 5 internal devs who have recently debugged p99 spikes; give them 30–45 min tasks: find the top 2 latency culprits and propose 1 mitigation. Log time-to-detect and perceived usefulness.
- Run 2 customer sessions with early access partners (private beta) and gather feedback on privacy defaults and suggestion accuracy.

Notes to self / TODO before next iteration:
- Add a minimal JSON schema example for the token-event payload and include in the infra PR.
- Create a short recording (Loom) showing the intended scrubber interactions; attach to the Confluence spec.
- Draft suggestion rule definitions (3 initial rules) and store them in product/optimize repo.

End of notes.

Appendix (quick glossary):
- token_event: single emitted token record with timing and meta.
- phase: a sub-stage of token processing (queue, forward, decode, KV, postprocess).
- kernel_id: identifier of the inference kernel used (helps identify quantization / fp usage).
- cache_hit: boolean flag for whether KV cache returned results for that token.
